result.answer: The agreement is the Information Services Agreement (ISA), which makes Google's search engine the default on Apple's products [by_paragraph-a24824e8067ab1df5b4f3671793252365777bfcc261a661196051fdf9e20f541].

context:
[by_paragraph-a24824e8067ab1df5b4f3671793252365777bfcc261a661196051fdf9e20f541 | https://www.theverge.com/2023/9/26/23891037/apple-eddy-cue-testimony-us-google | page 1]
Apple is in court because of something called the Information Services Agreement, or ISA: a deal that makes Google’s search engine the default on Apple’s products. The ISA has been in place since 2002, but Cue was responsible for negotiating its current iteration with Google CEO Sundar Pichai in 2016. In testimony today, the Justice Department grilled Cue about the specifics of the deal.

[by_paragraph-0ea348a1ae6676c97c8fa5f6bc1bce04fd969845aae3e561e2cf0b436c0c6683 | https://www.theverge.com/2023/9/26/23891037/apple-eddy-cue-testimony-us-google | page 1]
Cue was on the stand as a witness in US v. Google, the landmark antitrust trial over Google’s search business. Cue is one of the highest-profile witnesses in the case so far, in part because the deal between Google and Apple — which makes Google the default search engine on all Apple devices and pays Apple billions of dollars a year — is central to the US Department of Justice’s case against Google.

[by_paragraph-ac36e8b5bd3b0ae509460ffd5a2ca3448616d81cab8eafe027e89aa28a5dced1 | https://techcrunch.com/2023/11/13/more-from-the-us-v-google-trial-vertical-search-pre-installs-and-the-case-of-firefox-yahoo/ | page 1]
Rosenberg explained how Google gets manufacturers to sign a mobile app distribution agreement (MADA) that requires Android smartphone makers (like Samsung or Oppo) to pre-load a bundle of 11 Google apps on the device, including Search, Chrome and Play. They don’t have to be the default choices, he said.

[by_paragraph-b69d0cfa1a812399ebb50b607cbdf97728af49efe546ab5abab0b7f85f7f9adc | https://www.theverge.com/2023/9/26/23891037/apple-eddy-cue-testimony-us-google | page 1]
Cue acknowledged that the ISA didn’t allow Apple to offer users a choice of search engines during setup but also said he wouldn’t want to do that anyway. “We try to get people up and running as fast as possible,” he said. “Setup is just critical stuff.” Showing people a bunch of search engines they’ve never heard of would just be a bad user experience, he argued; even Cue couldn’t remember the names of some of the alternatives to Google. “We make Google be the default search engine,” he said, 

[by_paragraph-9e57222612c42af1d162597c4ada51d8b2a0fc808cabb279999407a2d500a09d | https://www.theverge.com/2023/9/26/23891037/apple-eddy-cue-testimony-us-google | page 1]
That question — whether Apple picked Google because it’s the most lucrative choice or the best product — was a key part of Cue’s testimony and, in fact, a key part of the DOJ’s entire case against Google. The Justice Department is focused on the deals Google makes — with Apple but also with Samsung and Mozilla and many others — to ensure it is the default search engine on practically every platform.
